note: The sharp keys round the circle (keys:2): D, A and E clockwise after G, then the sharp each one adds as the ringed 7th on its own staff, then the four sharps of E counted on the piano. The old Key choice on one staff is now three staffs side by side, since only the sharp keys fit the drill and "moves" can only open every key; the key is the lesson, so there are no moves.

exercise.title: The sharp keys, round the circle
exercise.why: Each key a 5th up keeps the sharps of the key before it and adds one more, on its 7th note, so the circle gives the sharp keys in order.

cells.text:
The circle of fifths below starts on G, the key with one sharp. Press D, the next key clockwise, then A and E after it. Read the number of sharps in the middle of the circle each time.
Each place clockwise is a 5th up, and adds one sharp.

The three staffs below show D, A and E major, the keys after G. On each one, tap up the scale from {{1}} and say each letter: the ringed {{7}} is the sharp this key adds, a half step under {{1}}.
Practice until you can name the new sharp before you tap it.

The piano below shows E major, four places clockwise from C. Tap up the scale from {{1}} and count the black keys: one for each sharp.
Then say the four sharps in the order the keys added them.
If the order slips, go back to the staffs above and read the ringed {{7}} of each key in turn.
